about.title: Monrovia Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products don't discriminate by neighborhood, and Monrovia residents run into them everywhere from Old Town shops to homes near Foothill and Huntington. A malfunctioning appliance, a car part that fails on I-210, faulty tools used on the job, or medication with an undisclosed risk can turn an ordinary day into a trip to the ER. California law gives injured consumers a real advantage here: strict liability generally means you don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. That said, these cases hinge on evidence, especially the product itself, which should be kept safe and unaltered. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your case directly. We simply listen to what happened, then connect you free of charge with an independent California attorney who works on contingency, so there's no upfront cost while you focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Product Liability Claim

items.title: Strict Liability Can Work in Your Favor
items.desc: Under California law, you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused your injury. An attorney can help identify which type of defect applies to your situation.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the retailer that sold the product can potentially be held liable. An attorney can help sort out who was involved in getting the defective product into your hands.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Because these claims often depend on physical evidence, keeping the product exactly as it was at the time of injury can be critical. An attorney can advise you on how to protect that evidence before it's lost or discarded.

items.question: I already threw away the packaging — do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Not necessarily a dealbreaker, but the product itself and any remaining components matter most. If you still have the item, store it somewhere safe and avoid using or repairing it. An attorney can advise on what other evidence, like receipts or photos, might help.

items.question: Do most product defect injuries in Monrovia involve car accidents?
items.answer: Not exclusively, but with corridors like I-210 and Foothill seeing regular traffic and 193 injury collisions reported in the most recent year, defective vehicle parts, tires, or safety systems can factor into some crashes. Household products, tools, and medical devices are common sources of injury too. An attorney can help figure out whether a product defect played a role in your specific incident.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer knew about the defect?
items.answer: Generally, no. California's strict liability standard typically focuses on whether the product itself was defective and caused harm, not on what the manufacturer knew or intended. This can make the path to holding a company accountable more direct than in a typical negligence case.
